response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) as avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) as total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: "Ignoring missing values" refers to standard SQL aggregation semantics where AVG() and SUM() exclude NULL values from calculations, not an instruction to filter out rows with NULL rebrate or rebtotal before grouping.
SQLite's default DESC sort order (which places NULLs last) satisfies the "missing last" requirement; no explicit NULLS LAST syntax is needed.

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignoring missing values" means exclude fees rows where rebrate or rebtotal are NULL before aggregating (stricter filtering).
alternatives.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) as avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) as total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND f.rebrate IS NOT NULL AND f.rebtotal IS NOT NULL GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC LIMIT 10
